instructions: In a small bowl, whisk the 1/3 cup almond milk, 2 tbsp nutritional yeast, 1/2 tsp Dijon, 1/4 tsp turmeric, 1/4 tsp cumin, 1/2 tsp salt and the garlic.
Pat the tofu dry with a clean towel and crumble it into bite-sized pieces with your fingers.
Dice the onion. That should be about 1/2 cup.
Heat 1 tbsp of the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the onion with a pinch of pepper and cook for about 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's soft and see-through.
Add the tofu and cook for 3 to 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's hot all the way through.
Meanwhile, toast the 4 slices of sourdough until they're golden and crisp.
Turn the heat down to low and pour the almond milk mixture over the tofu. Cook for 3 minutes, stirring now and then, until the tofu is evenly yellow and the liquid has cooked in.
Taste it, and add a pinch more pepper or salt if it's flat.
Drizzle the rest of the olive oil over the toast and spoon the scramble on top. Serve right away.
method_notes: Both read versions crumble extra firm tofu into a skillet of softened onion and season it with turmeric, cumin, garlic and salt. Love and Lemons (the lead) whisks almond milk, nutritional yeast, garlic, Dijon and the spices into a sauce that goes in at the end over low heat, and serves four from a 14 oz block. Minimalist Baker presses the tofu for 15 minutes, cooks red pepper and kale with it, and uses a water and spice sauce with chili powder. This one follows the lead and serves it on sourdough drizzled with olive oil, with no butter or dairy so it stays vegan.
